messages.subject: Running CIM with multiple phenotypes
messages.body_plain:
I have a quick question. Is it possible to implement mapping on
multiple traits at once with composite interval mapping? For scanone,
I can run multiple phenotypes using pheno.col, such as
pheno.col=1:5000. This is computationally efficient, especially when
parallelizing across multiple processors using snow. However, I cannot
figure out how to do this with cim from the R/qtl documentation. I
tried running cim in a loop instead, but found it to be very
inefficient and suck up a lot of computer time.

Thank you very much,

David

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Running CIM with multiple phenotypes
messages.body_plain:
Since CIM includes a forward selection for marker covariates that would be specific to each trait, there won't be a super efficient method for handling multiple phenotypes.

I would use a for loop with snow.  I'm not sure why it's especially inefficient.

Also note that the cim() function in R/qtl is quite crude; I'd prefer to use stepwiseqtl() with additive.only=TRUE, but that's probably even less efficient.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Running CIM with multiple phenotypes
messages.body_plain:
Something like this:

data(fake.bc)
n.orig.phe <- nphe(fake.bc)
n.new.phe <- 1000
fake.bc$pheno <- cbind(fake.bc$pheno,
                       matrix(rnorm(nind(fake.bc)*n.new.phe),
                              ncol=n.new.phe))
fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=2.5)

library(parallel)
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
mc.cores <- detectCores()

cim4parallel <- function(phe, ...) cim(pheno.col=phe, ...)

result <- mclapply(1:n.new.phe + n.orig.phe, cim4parallel, cross=fake.bc,
                   method="hk", n.marcovar=5, window=25, imp.method="imp",
                   mc.cores=mc.cores)

messages.subject: Coding data as F2 intercross?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I wanted to revisit this topic but ask about a different set of genotypes.

I have a set of ~4400 markers that are AA/AB in the female/male parents and I also have genotype data for 176 F2 individuals and 16 F1 individuals.

Using this data, I would like to see if there is a difference in recombination frequency between F1 males and females. To do this though, I first have to create a linkage map for these markers so that I can see which markers are on the same linkage group.

My question is: would it be possible to use the F2-intercross option in read.cross() to build a linkage map with this data? (1=AA, 2=AB, 3=BB)

Thank you!

Elisa

On Thursday, April 11, 2013 5:38:56 PM UTC-7, Elisa Zhang wrote:

> Hi Karl,
>
> I have a set of ~1200 markers that are AA/CD in the female/male parents respectively, and I also have the genotype data for 16 F1 individuals.
>
> Using this data, I would like to see if there is a difference in recombination frequency between males and females. To do this though, I was first planning to create a linkage map for these markers so that I can see which markers are on the same linkage group.
>
> My question is: would it be possible to use the 4-way cross option in read.cross() to build an accurate linkage map with this 3-way cross data? (I would only use the "1=AC" and "3=AD" coding scheme when reading in my genotype data).
>
> If an accurate linkage map can be created in this way, I can use the calculated recombination rate between markers to infer the phase of paternal-derived markers, and ultimately the recombination frequency in males vs females.
>
> Thanks for your help!
>
> Elisa

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Coding data as F2 intercross?
messages.body_plain:
I would try to use *all* of your markers and not focus on subsets with a particular pattern in the parents.

And I would try to work out phase in the F1 individuals so that the each cross between two F1 individuals could be treated as a phase-known 4-way cross.

I don't think you could just treat it as an intercross.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Coding data as F2 intercross?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

Thanks.

Do you have any suggestions for how to figure out phase in the F1 individuals?

Because the whole reason why I wanted to build this linkage map was so that I could figure out phase. I planned to make a linkage map so I would know which markers belong on a certain linkage group and could therefore use haplotype information for a pair of markers in the F2  to infer the phase of this pair of markers in the F1.

For example, if I only looked at F2 individuals whose parents were AA/AB (female/male respectively), and I saw that for a certain pair of markers, 50% of the F2 individuals were AB, AB at that pair and the other 50% were AA,AA, then I can infer that the A's of these 2 markers were on the same allele in the F1 parent and the B's were on the other allele. (This is also why I only wanted to use markers whose genotypes were AA/AB in the parents)

Thank you again Karl.

Elisa

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] simulate genotypes with a specified linkage map
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] simulate genotypes with a specified linkage map
messages.body_plain:
You need to revise the map object to be a bunch of matrices with two duplicate rows.

Here's an example, using lapply()

    data(map10)
    map10 <- lapply(map10, function(a) rbind(a,a))
    x <- sim.cross(map10, type="4way", n.ind=500)

karl

On May 28, 2013, at 11:19 AM, lp <louis....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thanks for the help.
> One more question. After pulling the map from a read.cross() object, how can I designate sex specific maps(or really specify that the two are the same), so that I can run the 4way sim.cross?
>
> Thanks,
> LP

>
> On Tuesday, May 31, 2011 11:54:30 PM UTC-4, Karl Broman wrote:
> It is the sim.cross function that needs the map.  sim.map is one way to create a map, but if you have one that you want to use, sim.map wouldn't be of interest.
> The simplest way I've found to get a map suitable for simulating crosses is to create a data file for a cross with the map I want, load it with read.cross, and then use pull.map to grab the map.
>
> But if you want to create a map from scratch, I give some example code below that might help.
>
> karl
> ----
> # create a map with 3 chromosomes
> map <- list("1"=c("m1"=0, "m2"=10, "m3"=20, "m4"=30, "m5"=40),
>             "2"=c("m6"=0, "m7"=15, "m8"=30, "m9"=45),
>             "X"=c("m10"=0, "m11"=20, "m12"=30))
>
> # need sex-specific map to simulate 4-way cross
> #   (though here we assume same map in the two sexes)
> for(i in seq(along=map))
>   map[[i]] <- rbind(map[[i]], map[[i]])
>
> # ..but no recombination in males on X
> map[["X"]][2,] <- 0
>
> # indicate that the first two chromosomes are autosomes
> class(map[[1]]) <- class(map[[2]]) <- "A"
>
> # indicate that the last chromosome is the X chromosome
> class(map[["X"]]) <- "X"
>
> # simulate a 4-way cross
> x <- sim.cross(map, type="4way", n.ind=50)
>
>
